evidence: src/infrastructure/UserController.ts: `private userRepository: IUserRepository;` and the GET /users handler calls `this.userRepository.findAll().map((user) => ({ id: user.getId(), name: user.getName() }))`, which goes around the use-case layer that every other route uses
src/infrastructure/TaskController.ts: all four routes go through use cases (createTaskUseCase, listTasksUseCase, assignTaskUseCase, markTaskDoneUseCase)

The same catch block `error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown error"; res.status(400).json({ error: message })` appears in ProjectController.ts (1x), TaskController.ts (4x) and UserController.ts (1x)
The same `if (!name) { res.status(400).json({ error: "Name is required" }); return; }` check appears in both ProjectController.ts and UserController.ts
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Taken together, the module is a sensible infrastructure adapter layer. It has in-memory repositories, Express controllers, a composition root (app.ts) and an entry point (server.ts), so the concern itself is cohesive. Two problems break the rubric.

1. Bypassed abstraction. Every route in ProjectController and TaskController goes through an application use case, and so does UserController's POST /users. UserController's GET /users does not. It keeps its own `userRepository` field, calls `this.userRepository.findAll()` directly and shapes the response inline with `{ id: user.getId(), name: user.getName() }`. That handler bypasses the use-case pattern the rest of the module uses and puts presentation logic in a different place from every other endpoint.

2. Duplicated rule. The rule for turning errors into HTTP responses is copied into each route handler rather than kept in one place, such as a shared error handler or Express error middleware. The copied code is `catch (error) { const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown error"; res.status(400).json({ error: message }); }`, and it appears once in ProjectController, four times in TaskController and once in UserController. Input validation is also repeated: the same `if (!name) { res.status(400).json({ error: "Name is required" }) }` check appears in both ProjectController and UserController.

violations.message: The GET /users handler skips the use-case layer. It calls `this.userRepository.findAll()` directly and builds the response DTO inline, while every other controller route delegates to an application use case.

The rule mapping errors to HTTP 400 (`error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown error"` followed by `res.status(400)`) is copied into all four route handlers instead of living in one shared error handler.
Repeats the same error-to-400 catch block and the same `Name is required` validation found in UserController, so these rules are duplicated across files.
